newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP says buys into French car parts maker Valeo.
newsitem.headline: CGIP says buys into French car parts maker Valeo.

text.p: French holding group CGIP is buying 20.2 percent of the capital and 19.5 percent of voting rights of Valeo to become the French car parts maker's leading shareholder, Valeo said in a statement on Tuesday.

The statement said state-owned bank Caisse des Depots et Consignation (CDC) was raising its Valeo stake to 5.4 percent from 1.9 percent and that JP Morgan and GT Corporation were in total buying 3.6 percent.
They are buying from Cerus, a company belonging to Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti which put its 28 percent up for grabs nearly a year ago.

Valeo said its board had also decided to make an exceptional dividend downpayment of 10 francs ($1.95) and that the payment of this sum would be handled from November 18 by French bank Credit du Nord.

Cerus said separately it would get 6.5 billion francs from all the stake sales including the advance dividend downpayment, with the possibility of another 0.2 billion francs in further dividend payments.
